sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2025
sources.description: Current full release. Announced at OWASP Global AppSec Washington D.C., November 2025; final published text released January 2026 — fully current as of 2026-07. New: A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures, A10:2025 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions. SSRF folded into A01 Broken Access Control; A09 renamed Security Logging and Alerting Failures. Supersedes the 2021 edition.

sources.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS) 5.0
sources.description: ASVS 5.0.0 released May 30, 2025. First major update since 4.0 (2019). ~350 requirements across 17 chapters; expanded API, SPA, and microservice coverage; action-oriented requirements; clarifies that black-box testing alone is insufficient for most controls. Supersedes ASVS 4.0.3.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
sources.description: Separate from LLM Top 10. Announced 2025-12-09 (OWASP GenAI Security Project, Black Hat Europe / OWASP Agentic Security Summit); officially released and current as of 2026-07. Ten categories, prefix ASI01-ASI10: planning, tool use, identity, supply chain, code execution, memory, inter-agent communication, cascading failures, human-agent trust, rogue agents.

sources.title: OpenGrep
sources.description: Community fork of Semgrep Community Edition (LGPL-2.1), launched January 2025 after Semgrep moved cross-function taint analysis to its commercial platform. Backed by Aikido, Endor Labs, Jit, Orca Security. Fully backward-compatible with Semgrep rule format, JSON, and SARIF output. No paid tier.

sources.title: Trivy Supply Chain Compromise Advisory (2026-03-19)
sources.description: 2026-03-19: threat actor (attributed to TeamPCP) used compromised credentials to publish a malicious Trivy v0.69.4 release, force-push 75 of 76 version tags in aquasecurity/trivy-action to credential-stealing malware, and replace all 7 tags in aquasecurity/setup-trivy. Root cause: non-atomic credential rotation after an initial disclosure on 2026-03-01 left a valid token active for days. Malware exfiltrated SSH keys, cloud credentials, Kubernetes tokens, and env vars via HTTP POST to a typosquatted domain. Safe versions: Trivy 0.69.2/0.69.3+, trivy-action 0.35.0+, setup-trivy 0.2.6+ (recreated). Key lesson: because version TAGS themselves were force-pushed, a pin like `@0.28.0` is not inherently safe from this class of attack — pin to a release SHA digest, and verify with `gh attestation verify` where attestations exist.

sources.title: CVSS v4.0 (FIRST.org)
sources.description: Current CVSS major version, released November 2023. As of 2026, NVD publishes CVSS v4.0 alongside v3.1 for newly scored CVEs (official NVD support); historical CVEs keep their v3.1 score and are not being retroactively re-scored. Numeric severity bands (Critical 9.0-10, High 7.0-8.9, Medium 4.0-6.9, Low 0.1-3.9) are unchanged from v3.1, but the underlying vector-to-score computation differs (v4.0 adds Safety, Automatable, and Supplemental/Threat/Environmental metric groups and removes the old impact-subscore formula) — do not treat a v3.1 score and a v4.0 score for two different CVEs as directly comparable without checking which version produced each.

sources.title: EPSS - Exploit Prediction Scoring System (FIRST.org)
sources.description: FIRST.org SIG. Current model: EPSS v4 (model version 2025.03.14), publishing daily since 2025-03-17. Produces a 0-1 probability that a given CVE will be exploited in the wild in the next 30 days, using CVSS subscores, exploit-code availability, and threat-intel signals as features. Complements, does not replace, CVSS: CVSS scores technical severity if exploited; EPSS scores the probability of exploitation. Use both plus reachability for triage (see Vulnerability Management Workflow in SKILL.md).

sources.title: Betterleaks
sources.description: Open-source secrets scanner created 2026-02-03 by the original gitleaks author as gitleaks' de facto successor; co-maintained with long-time gitleaks contributors. Reached v1.1.1 by 2026-03-17 and v1.1.2 by 2026-04-08. gitleaks itself is now feature-complete (security patches only). Betterleaks is young (weeks old at last check) — pilot it alongside gitleaks rather than replacing gitleaks outright until it has a longer track record in your CI.

metadata.title: QA Security Testing - Sources
metadata.description: Automated security testing pipelines for SAST, DAST, SCA, secret scanning, and container scanning. Use when integrating security scanners into CI, triaging findings, setting vulnerability SLAs, or building security regression tests.

game_theory_security_testing.title: Tambe — Security and Game Theory (2011)
game_theory_security_testing.description: Stackelberg security game formalism with ARMOR (LAX) and IRIS (port) deployed systems. Foundation for scan-scheduling-as-security-game and red-team Stackelberg models.

game_theory_security_testing.title: Sandler & Arce — Terrorism and Game Theory (Simulation & Gaming 2003)
game_theory_security_testing.description: Attacker cost-benefit and timing models. Applicable to exploitation-window analysis and dependency scan cadence decisions (P4).

game_theory_security_testing.title: Gordon & Loeb — Economics of Information Security Investment (ACM TISSEC 2002)
game_theory_security_testing.description: Repeated-game investment framing for security testing cadence; dependency scanning frequency as marginal-value optimization.

game_theory_security_testing.title: MITRE ATT&CK Framework
game_theory_security_testing.description: Canonical tactic and technique taxonomy for red-team exercise scoring (R3) and ATT&CK coverage metric in anti-pattern A2.

game_theory_security_testing.title: CISA / MITRE ATT&CK Adversary Emulation Plans
game_theory_security_testing.description: Operationalized emulation plans grounding attacker behavior models used in red-team Stackelberg framing (P3) and scan scheduling (P1).

game_theory_security_testing.title: AFL++ Coverage-Guided Fuzzer
game_theory_security_testing.description: Coverage-guided fuzzing feedback loop that approximates multi-armed bandit exploration. Primary reference for fuzz seed selection pattern (P2) and R2.
